title: Isaiah McDuffie: Packers have everything we need
summary: The Packers have made it to the playoffs in each of the last three seasons, but their stays in the postseason have not been long ones.
full_text: The Packers have made it to the playoffs in each of the last three seasons, but their stays in the postseason have not been long ones. After winning in Dallas to kick off the 2023 playoffs, the team has lost their last three postseason outings. The most recent defeat saw them blow an 11-point lead against the Bears in the fourth quarter and led to questions about whether the team would move forward with head coach Matt LaFleur. LaFleur remains on the sideline and the team avoided major changes to the roster this offseason, but linebacker Isaiah McDuffie doesn't believe the team is missing anything they need to get over the hump in 2026 "I think we've got everything we need ," McDuffie said on NFL Network. "At the end of the day, it's just finishing. Getting late in the season, just finishing those games when we are up on guys, just putting the nail in the coffin." While the Packers opted against a major shakeup, they did bring in a new defensive coordinator when Jeff Hafley left to become Miami's head coach. McDuffie said that Jonathan Gannon "definitely brings that juice" and that "it's going to be fun to watch us" execute the things that Gannon has installed on that side of the ball. That prediction will be likelier to come true if Micah Parsons can return to full speed, but McDuffie and the rest of the Packers will have to keep things afloat until that happens.
author: Josh Alper

title: Ben Johnson: D'Andre Swift is already a vital part of Bears' offense, and capable of more
summary: "He's a dynamic player," Johnson said. "I've known that about him since he came into the league."
full_text: ''' Bears running back D'Andre Swift had a career-high 1,087 rushing yards and nine touchdowns last season, but coach Ben Johnson thinks Swift can do even more. Swift played his first three NFL seasons for the Lions while Johnson was on Detroit's coaching staff, and while the Lions decided to trade Swift away after drafting running back Jahmyr Gibbs, Johnson said he's always believed Swift is an elite playmaker with the ball in his hands. "He's a dynamic player," Johnson said, via the Bears' website. "I've known that about him since he came into the league, firsthand up there in Detroit, and certainly last year I wasn't surprised about the year he had. So, is he capable of more? Absolutely . He absolutely is. He's a vital part of what we do here." As much as the Bears' offense was celebrated last year for Johnson's trick plays and Caleb Williams' late-game heroics, Swift was one of the most effective running backs in the NFL in 2025. And Johnson expects more in 2026.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Lawyer says Ryan Gold didn't know Cardinals' draft picks
summary: In a statement issued to PFT and others on Sunday, attorney Mike Caspino said the allegations of gambling violations against Cardinals director of college scouting Ryan Gold are "blatantly false."
full_text: In a statement issued to PFT and others on Sunday, attorney Mike Caspino said the allegations of gambling violations against Cardinals director of college scouting Ryan Gold are " blatantly false ." Caspino elaborated on his position in comments to Adam Schefter of ESPN. As to the claim that Gold engaged in gambling on NFL games, Caspino said Gold's wife was making $10 bets per week with a group of high-school friends — and that Gold wasn't involved. As to the more serious allegation that Gold had shared inside information about the team's draft picks before they were announced, Caspino said that Gold didn't know the draft picks in advance, and that only owner Michael Bidwill and G.M. Monti Ossenfort had the information. The fact that Ossenfort came up in the Bill Belichick school of extreme secrecy makes this claim plausible. Some teams notoriously protect the identity of its draft picks, to the point of engaging in internal misdirection. In 2005, for example, then-Dolphins coach Nick Saban told staffers that the team would be using the second overall pick on Michigan receiver Braylon Edwards. Instead, Saban picked Auburn running back Ronnie Brown. Also, Chris Simms has explained on PFT Live that, during his time working for the Patriots, the room containing the draft board was closely protected from access to anyone other than an extremely small group of people. That said, there's still a lag between the time that the name is shared with the draft room and the moment the pick is announced. (It's unclear when the information was allegedly shared, relative to when the picks were announced.) Caspino has vowed to appeal. The outcome may hinge on whether Gold will get a fair and impartial hearing from a neutral party, or whether the league will be handling the second look at the decision the league has already made. Bet on the latter. (Actually don't bet; it's just a figure of speech.)
author: Mike Florio

title: Cam Skattebo doesn't care if people think he's "brain-dead"
summary: Giants running back Cam Skattebo attempted to show that his ankle is healed by attempting to perform a backflip on Saturday at Fanatics Fest.
full_text: Giants running back Cam Skattebo attempted to show that his ankle is healed by attempting to perform a backflip on Saturday at Fanatics Fest. Skattebo did not stick the landing . On Sunday, Skattebo and Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart appeared on a special episode of The Fantasy Footballers from SiriusXM. Skattebo addressed his Saturday shenanigans. “I mean, so I've been doing backflips since I was like four years old," Skattebo said. "So it's natural to me. I'm gonna address the elephant. I will not hurt myself before the season. . . ." He then explained his pratfall. "So what happened was, I don't know if you guys know WWE or not, those floors are bouncy," Skattebo said. "So when I took off, I was mid-air, like, 'Holy cow, I'm not gonna land this, I'm way too high.' Landed, but it had too much cushion. It wasn't a stiff, firm ground. So that's why I kinda like went back, safely landed, got back up, was good to go. So nothing came out from that. I'm perfectly fine. Nothing happened. We're good.” Some would say it's not good that Skattebo unnecessarily put himself at risk. He also was asked whether he enjoys being regarded as a "wild maniac." "I totally enjoy that part," Skattebo said. "I think I less enjoy the 'brain-dead kind of guy.' But it is what it is. I mean, the New York people love it, so I'm just gonna keep being me. And if they wanna say I'm brain-dead and I don't have no brain, then who cares? Fuck it, you know?” (Nothing says you have a brain more than saying, "I don't have no brain.") Back in March, Skattebo made waves by claiming that CTE, and asthma, aren’t real . He later apologized for his " tasteless joke ."
author: Mike Florio

title: Cardinals executive Ryan Gold's lawyer says gambling accusations are "blatantly false"
summary: Gold will appeal the indefinite suspension.
full_text: On Friday, the NFL announced that Cardinals director of college scouting Ryan Gold has been suspended indefinitely for violating the league's gambling policy. On Sunday, Gold's lawyer issued a statement denying the allegations. "Ryan Gold has been an outstanding NFL executive for over a decade," attorney Mike Caspino said. "The accusations made by the league, regarding his participation in prohibited gambling activities, are blatantly false. We have demanded an appeal and we look forward to clearing his good name." The league has accused Gold of providing inside information regarding the Cardinals’ draft selections before the picks were announced, and of participating in parlay bets on NFL and college games. Gold shouldn't expect any support from the Cardinals. The team said Friday that it " fully support[s] " the league's decision. The Cardinals also have deactivated Gold's bio page on the team's website.
author: Mike Florio

title: In the World Cup final, it's Spain over Argentina in extra time, 1-0
summary: Well, it's time to rip up the grass at MetLife Stadium.
full_text: Well, it's time to rip up the grass at MetLife Stadium. Spain defeated Argentina in New Jersey on Sunday, 1-0, for the 2026 World Cup crown. Spain dominated throughout the match, but Argentina kept Spain from scoring through 90 minutes of regulation. After losing Enzo Fernández to a red card after he got his second yellow card of the match in second-half stoppage time, Argentina got through the first half of extra time without giving up a goal despite being down a man. Early in the second half of extra time, Nico Williams used a header while running toward the goal line to set up Ferran Torres for the only goal of the game. Argentina still had a chance or two to send the game to penalty kicks. The best opportunity came when Giuliano Simeone had a clear shot at the goal but sent it high over the crossbar. Spain get their first World Cup title since 2010, while also preventing Argentina from becoming the first back-to-back winner since Brazil in 1958 and 1962. And that's that for the World Cup. Just in time for American football training camps to open.
author: Mike Florio

title: Authorities will explore whether Saquon Barkley burglary was part of a broader ring
summary: Two years after multiple NFL stars had their residences burglarized while they weren't home, the home of Eagles running back Saquon Barkley was invaded on Saturday while he and his family were inside.
full_text: Two years after multiple NFL stars had their residences burglarized while they weren't home, the home of Eagles running back Saquon Barkley was invaded on Saturday while he and his family were inside. In addition to trying to solve the case, the authorities will attempt to determine whether the incident is connected to any of the criminal groups that target athletes. " We will look at all angles of this because we know, obviously, it's been all over the news in the past few years about different professional athletes' homes getting burglarized," Capt. Tyler Moyer of the Tredyffrin Township Police Department told WCAU-TV, via ESPN. At least one suspect entered Barkley's home. "They were home, and fortunately, as you know, with any situation like this, our main concern is that the residents of that home at the time were unharmed, which they were," Moyer told reporters. "They were fine afterwards, obviously unsettled as anyone would be." Police are searching for at least two suspects. In 2024, Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce, and Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow were among the victims of a crime ring that has since been disrupted, with multiple arrests.
author: Mike Florio

title: Southern coach Marshall Faulk: NFL is no longer the "next level" for HBCU talent
summary: For decades, the best of the best players from HBCU schools found their next opportunities in the NFL.
full_text: For decades, the best of the best players from HBCU schools found their next opportunities in the NFL. Times have changed, dramatically. Hall of Fame running back Marshall Faulk, the new head coach at Southern University, recently explained the changed circumstances for HBCU players. “I believe that the next level is no longer the NFL ,” Faulk said recently during SWAC Football Media Day, via Steven J. Gaither of HBCU Gameday . “We get poached by the FBS. They want our players.” That's one of the basic realities of the new era of NIL and the transfer portal. Once it's clear that players at HBCU programs can perform at a high level, high-level college programs will come calling. “They have an opportunity to maybe go somewhere and make good money while they’re in college,” Faulk said. “The game has changed. The landscape of college football has changed.” In past years, this would have meant Hall of Fame players like Walter Payton, Jerry Rice, Aeneas Williams, Jackie Slater, Michael Strahan, Shannon Sharpe, Mel Blount, John Stallworth, and Deacon Jones landing quickly at major college programs — and making significant money. Now, the best players at HBCU programs will get opportunities to play, and to get paid, by some of the programs with real money to spend while further honing their skills before a chance to perform in the NFL.
author: Mike Florio

title: Mother Nature cooperates with FIFA for World Cup finale
summary: The World Cup ends today, with the final match between Spain and Argentina.
full_text: The World Cup ends today, with the final match between Spain and Argentina. And the folks at FIFA got very lucky with the weather. The wildfire smoke is gone, and there will be no rain on Spain. Is MetLife Stadium truly the best place for the last game? SoFi Stadium is superior. Even AT&T Stadium and Mercedes-Benz Stadium would have made more sense, since they're covered. Picking New Jersey in mid-July was always a roll of the dice, similar to the NFL's decision to play Super Bowl XLVIII there in early 2014. It could have been very hot today. (It'll be in the low 80s.) It could have been ridiculously humid. (It's only 44 percent.) There's zero chance of thunderstorms or rain of any kind. The game begins at 3:00 p.m. ET on Fox. (The Spanish-language version is on Telemundo and Peacock.) I'm heading to the barn to watch it on the big screen with a big cigar and a small workload. The best part about truly discovering soccer this summer has been enjoying a sport for the sake of the sport, without having to chase stories or formulate takes or whatever. Not that I don't love that aspect of this existence; it's just nice to be a sports fan and only a sports fan — especially of a sport that it took me more than 50 years of watching sports to truly appreciate and understand (mostly). If you're near a TV today, or if you're simply watching on your phone, check it out. It will be a spectacle. And hopefully it will be a great game between the top two teams in the world.

title: The Cardinals don't have a quarterback competition, in theory (but maybe they will)
summary: The Cardinals don't have a quarterback competition.
full_text: The Cardinals don't have a quarterback competition. In theory. But a competition possibly could emerge. Jacoby Brissett is the starter. He's not happy with a contract that paid him to be a backup. The Cardinals have yet to adjust his contract to compensate him fairly to be the QB1. Brissett stayed away from the voluntary portion of the offseason program. He reported, as required, for the mandatory minicamp. He'll presumably show up for training camp. But what will he do when he gets there? Starting quarterbacks typically do more than just show up and do the minimum. They put in extra work. They do other things. They are, for many teams, a member of management who operates among the workers, operating as a de facto player-coach. Will Brissett embrace the extra stuff, if he's not happy with his contract? Really, why go above and beyond the basic requirements of the job if you're not being paid fairly to do the job? Then there's the chance he'll hold in, not practicing at all until he gets a revised contract. Complicating the situation is that Brissett represents himself. Which necessarily makes the negotiations more delicate and potentially awkward. If Brissett the agent advises Brissett the client to punch the clock and go home (or to decline to practice), it opens the door for one of the other quarterbacks to fill the void. Whether it's Gardner Minshew or rookie Carson Beck (or a little of both) remains to be seen. But it could be that Brissett will choose not to operate at all times (or at all) like the starter unless and until he's compensated like a veteran starter. The Cardinals can easily avoid that outcome by figuring out a fair number for Brissett to be the starter. The range for veteran starters is currently broad, starting in the low 20s and extending into the mid-60s. Under the two-year deal Brissett signed in 2025, his average annual salary is $6.25 million. On one level, it's madness. At another level, there's a potential method to it. Stuck in a division with a trio of Super Bowl contenders, the Cardinals face a steep uphill climb to a playoff berth. It will be far easier to accept their fate for 2026 and sink in the standings — while rising in the draft order for 2027. Which sets the Cardinals up for the ability to draft one of the best quarterbacks in next year's crop. (Unless and until Arch Manning makes it clear he's not interested in playing there.) Even if Brissett keeps the starting job (with or without an adjustment to his contract), it seems inevitable that Beck will get a chance to play. The Cardinals need to know whether he's got the potential to be a year-to-year starter before committing to drafting a quarterback next year. If you think they won't, remember that they took Kyler Murray with the first pick one year after trading up to No. 10 to draft Josh Rosen. (While also passing on Lamar Jackson.) So, no, there's officially no quarterback competition in Arizona. But if Brissett chooses not to accept the mantle of being the starter until he's paid like one, a competition could unfold.
author: Mike Florio

title: Cam Skattebo's failed Fanatics Fest backflip tempts fate
summary: For some football players, the attitude that makes them great on the field can tempt them to do dumb things off the field.
full_text: For some football players, the attitude that makes them great on the field can tempt them to do dumb things off the field. Case in point: Giants running back Cam Skattebo. In November, not long after he suffered a season-ending ankle injury, he was pushing and shoving at a WWE event. Now that his ankle has healed, Skattebo wanted to prove it during an appearance at Fanatics Fest. After pulling up the leg of his pants to expose the ankle that had been dislocated (along with a tibia fracture), Skattebo did a backflip . He didn't stick the landing. Skattebo stumbled backward and fell, before springing up and acting like he meant to do that. As many have suggested, Giants coach John Harbaugh may not be thrilled when he sees the video. And while some have pointed out that Harbaugh once yelled at quarterback Joe Flacco for riding a skateboard during the playoff run that resulted in a Ravens Super Bowl win, it wasn't Harbaugh — it was former G.M. Ozzie Newsome . Regardless, it's a valid concern. Even if Skattebo will eventually be taking much greater risks with his health when it's time to get hit and tackled, there's no reason to add to the risks by doing other things that could result in an injury.
author: Mike Florio

title: There's no word yet on in-season Hard Knocks
summary: In 2024 and 2025, the selected division was known by June.
full_text: '' It's been known since March that the Seahawks will be the preseason Hard Knocks team for 2026 — and that the Patriots will finally take their Hard Knocks turn in 2027. It's not yet known which teams will take center stage for in-season Hard Knocks . In 2024, the in-season version expanded its focus from one team to a full division, in part to dilute the competitive impact of the intrusion during a time when the games count. The first year, the series tracked the teams of the AFC North. Last year, it was the NFC East. This year, there's been no announcement yet. The 2025 teams were announced in May. In 2024, the NFL disclosed the division in June. We've made multiple attempts over the past week to get an answer as to when the teams will be known. To date, there's no indication as to when the division will be disclosed — or if there will even be an in-season Hard Knocks in 2026. There are three potential explanations for the silence. One, they've decided not to announce the division in advance. Two, they've yet to pick the division. Three, they've decided not to do it at all. The in-season version gets easily lost in the shuffle, especially as the league shuffles around its schedule to maximize standalone windows. With games to watch on Thursdays, Sundays, Mondays, and (this year) multiple Wednesdays and multiple Fridays, would enough people watch a weekly look at four different teams? If it happens this year, the practical options are down to four divisions. With a team from the NFC West serving as the focal point for Hard Knocks this year and a team from the AFC East doing it next year, those two divisions presumably aren't in play. That leaves the AFC South, the AFC West, the NFC North, or the NFC South. Or maybe the plug has quietly been pulled on the whole thing. If shifting to a full division was aimed at avoiding putting one team at a disadvantage in its own division, the full division ends up at a disadvantage in comparison to the other teams in the conference with which the Hard Knocks teams are competing for wild-card berths and playoff positioning. (Especially if the league is moving toward a new seeding structure that doesn't guarantee a home game for a division winner, which is expected to happen when the season expands to 18 games.) Maybe, just like the offseason version of Hard Knocks (which was so revealing and compelling when the Giants did it in 2024 that no one else will do it), Hard Knocks will be reverting to a preseason exercise only. There's another possible outcome, in our view. In lieu of rolling out the in-season Hard Knocks episodes during the season, maybe the time to unveil the series will be the upcoming offseason. It doesn't hurt the Quarterback series that the show arrives months after the prior season ended, when there's nothing else going on for NFL fans to consume. Frankly, the best approach would be to capture the raw audio and video as to all teams, and to decide after the season ends which division provides the most interesting subject for the series. Or, if the cameras and microphones will be present for all teams, why not put together an in-season series that looks at the most interesting moments from the full league? However it goes, it's an NFL decision and not an ESPN call. NFL Films remained with the NFL after the ESPN merger with NFL Media. For the NFL, the ultimate business decision could come down to whether it makes business sense to not do in-season Hard Knocks at all — or whether it makes more sense to embrace a more ambitious project that entails getting footage from 32 teams and editing an after-the-fact Hard Knocks that could have much more appeal than focusing on one division, while also eliminating any concerns about competitive disadvantage.

title: 2026 NFL training camp report dates, joint practices, top storyline for all 32 teams
summary: With training camps less than a week away, here's a team-by-team look at the battles, injuries, quarterback questions and breakout candidates that will shape the 2026 NFL season
full_text:
For all the excitement of free agency and the NFL Draft and all the tea-leaf reading of OTAs, training camp is when things really get real. There are roster battles, depth chart battles and starting job battles. There will be plenty of roster churn as teams evaluate themselves and outside options. There will be feel-good stories about unlikely players making the roster, and there will be surprising cuts. Tempers will flare, and some joint practices will be far more important than the actual preseason games.
Below is every team's training camp schedule, the joint practice schedule -- joint practices are often the most revealing part of camp -- and finally every team's top training camp storyline as the season nears.
After career lows in catches and yards, DJ Moore landed in Buffalo, where he is immediately the clear No. 1 wide receiver. He still has his downfield chops, and that is crucial for a Bills offense that leaned heavily into short passing last year. Can Moore be the top guy for Josh Allen in a successful passing offense? How willing is new coach Joe Brady, last year's offensive coordinator, to become more aggressive?
The Dolphins are an extremely young team in the wake of tearing things down to the studs. But they also took a swing on Malik Willis, who played well as a backup in Green Bay. Miami is not Green Bay, though. Willis has arguably the NFL's worst supporting cast, with pretty much no proven wide receivers and several question marks on the offensive line.
For all the upgrades New England made, none are as big as A.J. Brown. The star wide receiver should be exactly what Drake Maye needs after his breakout season, a big wide receiver with downfield bona fides and the ability to win on in-breaking routes. If they can establish a good rapport early, both should be in for big seasons. Brown's health is worth watching.
Rookies look to carve out roles
The Jets used their three first-round picks on players who should contribute immediately: EDGE David Bailey , tight end Kenyon Sadiq and wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr . For a team looking at a bridge year with a roster filled with intriguing youngsters and solid veterans on short-term deals, the youngsters will be the focus as the Jets look to build momentum.
Lamar Jackson's contract situation, fit in new offense
For the first time in nearly two decades, the Ravens have a new coach. Jesse Minter should be an immediate boost for the Ravens' defense, which has had spells of excellent play and spells of very poor play seemingly every year. But Lamar Jackson will have all the eyes on him once again. New offensive coordinator Declan Doyle will place him under center more than he's used to, and there's also the contract extension issue looming in the background.
The Bengals made big splashes at defensive line ( Dexter Lawrence ), EDGE ( Boye Mafe , second-round pick Cashius Howell ) and safety ( Bryan Cook ). Last year's first-round pick, EDGE Shemar Stewart , is in the midst of his first full NFL offseason and was always going to be a developmental guy; can he make the jump? The Bengals simply need their defense to be mediocre, not among the NFL's worst.
Shedeur Sanders vs. Deshaun Watson
For a team as early into yet another rebuild as the Browns are, this, on the surface, looks to be a strange quarterback battle. Shedeur Sanders is much younger and, though he struggled massively as a rookie, he had some nice moments and produced some big plays in exceedingly poor circumstances. Deshaun Watson, though, has more experience in systems like new coach Todd Monken's. Either way, viable quarterback play is important for the Browns to at least judge their youngsters at every other offensive position.
New-look offense looks to improve
Aaron Rodgers is back after a middling-at-best season (24th in net yards per attempt, 33rd in air yards per attempt). Was his overreliance on quick, short throws all on him? The Steelers traded for Michael Pittman Jr. and Germie Bernard , which should help unlock DK Metcalf downfield ... if Rodgers is willing to hang in and make some throws. Up front, Troy Fautanu slides from right tackle to left tackle. In the backfield, Rico Dowdle joins Jaylen Warren . Can Mike McCarthy make it all work?
Revamped offensive line, run game
The Texans have a championship-level defense. On offense, C.J. Stroud has to rebound from a tough 2025. One of the best ways for him to do that is the Texans' investments on the offensive line ( Keylan Rutledge , Braden Smith , Wyatt Teller ) and at running back (traded for David Montgomery ), paying dividends. Houston was 30th in rushing success rate.
Coming off a torn Achilles, Daniel Jones has worked his way back to 7-on-7 drills but hasn't taken part in 11-on-11 this offseason. Fear not, Colts fans: There's still a long way to go until the season, and Jones has maintained he is on track for Week 1. When training camp arrives, Jones' readiness from a health and performance standpoint will be key.
Hunter played roughly twice as many offensive snaps as he did defensive snaps in a rookie year cut short due to injury. His best game -- eight catches, 101 yards, one touchdown -- was, unfortunately, also his final one of the season. The Jaguars have more depth at wide receiver than they do at cornerback.
Like many of his fellow 2025 rookie quarterbacks who got legit playing time, Cam Ward had some impressive moments but mostly struggled. The Titans made significant upgrades on the offensive side of the ball, led by No. 4 overall pick Carnell Tate . The offensive line remains iffy, though, and Ward's first order of business will be to cut down on negative plays.
Bo Nix required a second surgery on his ankle earlier this year, and while the expectation is he'll be ready for training camp, his recovery is very much worth monitoring. He'll also have a new play caller in Davis Webb , who has those responsibilities for the first time. How Nix manages the injury recovery, the new play caller and getting on the same page as new wide receiver Jaylen Waddle bears monitoring.
Patrick Mahomes ' recovery
The expectation is for Patrick Mahomes to be ready for training camp, but what level of "ready" is he? Will he partake in every part of practice, or every practice period? Will he be on a pitch count? Mahomes isn't the most fleet of foot, but he is a wily, effective scrambler, and his pocket movement is a massive part of his game. This is his first major injury.
With apologies to some very good players the Raiders have -- namely Maxx Crosby , Brock Bowers , Tyler Linderbaum and (potentially) Ashton Jeanty -- Fernando Mendoza is the storyline. How many reps does he get, and how does that number change over the days and weeks of training camp? How does he look? How long can Kirk Cousins hold him off?
Welcome to the Mike McDaniel show
The Chargers have new coordinators on both sides of the ball, but the Mike McDaniel addition will be the more drastic change of the two. He's a run-game mastermind who also has excellent offensive creativity overall, and he could help take Justin Herbert , Omarion Hampton and Ladd McConkey to the next level.
How much better is the defense?
The Cowboys used five of their seven picks on defense, headlined by first-round selections Caleb Downs and Malachi Lawrence . They also traded for Dee Winters and Rashan Gary and added Jalen Thompson and Cobie Durant. The most important addition might be defensive coordinator Christian Parker. Dallas also has Quinnen Williams for a full season. How quickly does it all come together, and is there enough talent, even with the perceived upgrades?
Jaxson Dart didn't start until Week 4 last year and, like most young players with talent, he produced some fun highs and some not-so-fun lows, the latter of which included several hard hits taken and one concussion sustained. title: Eagles' Saquon Barkley, family unharmed after attempted home invasion
summary: The alleged suspects left Barkley's home prior to police arriving at the running back's home
full_text:
Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley and his family were not harmed following an attempted home invasion Saturday morning, per the Tredyffrin Township Police Department .
The incident happened around 5 a.m., according to the Chester County District Attorney's Office . Police are in pursuit of a white SUV and two suspects they believe participated in the alleged crime, and at least one of the suspects entered the Barkley family's house while they were inside.
"We know there's more than one, but we're still trying to determine how many were involved," Captain Tyler Moyer of the Tredyffrin Township Police Department said, via NBC 10 Philadelphia . "All of the occupants in the home were physically OK, obviously a little unsettled as anybody would be, but nobody was harmed."
The district attorney's office currently believes nothing was taken during the alleged robbery.
"We are incredibly grateful that the Barkley family was not injured during this incident. We are asking the public to help us identify those responsible by checking any home security cameras for suspicious activity in the area around 5:00 a.m. If you saw anything unusual or have video that may assist investigators, please contact the Tredyffrin Township Police Department immediately," the D.A.'s office said in a statement on Facebook .
Barkley isn't the first NFL superstar to be targeted of late. Joe Burrow , Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce have also been targets. Four men were arrested in Jan. 2025 in connection with a burglary at Burrow's home. In February 2025, the United States charged seven people in connection to burglaries of Burrow, Mahomes, Los Angeles Laker star Luka Doncic, Minnesota Timberwolves guard Mike Conley Jr., Tyler Seguin of the Dallas Stars and Bobby Portis of the Miami Heat.
That's why police are working in tandem with federal law enforcement to determine if this attempted burglary was connected to those of other high-profile athletes.
"We will look at all angles of this because we know, obviously, it's been all over the news in the past few years about different professional athletes' homes getting burglarized," Moyer said.

full_text: The Arizona Cardinals are on the verge of opening up training camp. Most NFL clubs require the rookies to show up earlier, but the Cardinals’ rookies and veterans both show up on July 22. This training camp has a lot riding on during the preseason. A new head coach, Mike LaFleur, plus a new offensive scheme, is being installed. RELATED: THE RECEIVER NOBODY IS TALKING ABOUT Ahead of training camp opening, let’s look at the receiver room. This year’s group has a lot riding on it. There should be a lot of improvement with this group. New this year is Kendrick Bourne, signed during free agency from the San Francisco 49ers, Reggie Virgil, who was chosen in Round 5 of the NFL draft, along with undrafted rookie Harrison Wallace, III. Cardinals WR depth chart Right outside receiver: Michael Wilson, backup Fehoko, Jalen Brooks, Harrison Wallace, III Left outside receiver: Marv Harrison, Jr., backup Reggie Virgil, Xavier Weaver, Bryson Green Slot receiver: Kendrick Bourne, backup Devin Duvernay, Tejhaun Palmer, Ihmir Smith-Marsette Best expectations? Wilson had a coming-out year last season and has solidified the WR1 position. He is in line to get an extension, which should occur during training camp. He led all receivers last year in total yards with 1,006 yards and was the second most on the roster behind Trey McBride in targets with 126. With this new offense, expect a Pro Bowl year with Wilson. Harrison and Bourne, while neither broke the 1,000-yard hurdle last season, should be able to move the needle and display why their skills will need to increase their production this year. Harrison needs to prove why he was selected #4 overall, and Bourne should provide good hands with the slot position. Duvernay, Weaver, and Fehoko, plus the rookie Virgil, reward the Cardinals for showing patience and confidence in their abilities. This group can shine if the correct quarterback is found early enough. Worst case? Harrison’s sophomore slump becomes a sign of a complete unraveling, and Wilson shows his best effort was a one-off. Retreads of Duvernay and Bourne can’t get any production in the short game this new offense offers, and the rookie Virgil shows why he dropped to Round 5 before being selected. 2026 version? This group will love this new offense. It doesn’t throw deep much, but the talent is there with the few plays that do go long. It is geared for the short to intermediate game. Yards for stats won’t be generated in large chunks but in steady increments. The squad will rely heavily on both Wilson and Harrison, with Bourne getting looks for the short game. The only questions will be who will be the other three players that will gain roster spots, and how they will be used in the game plan. Like any year, there could be a complete surprise that wasn’t expected. The top three assist in order to slot the secondary guys into positions that are more suited to their skills. Which is how you want it to be, as opposed to relying on guys who try hard but are limited in what they can bring to the field. This entire group has the opportunity to become amazing and electric.

How do the different positional groups in the division stack up to one another? Let’s rank the AFC North squads by position, continuing with linebacker. 1. Baltimore Ravens Starters : Roquan Smith, Teddye Buchanan Depth: Trenton Simpson, Carl Jones, Jay Higgins IV The Ravens made no additions to their core linebacker group this offseason. That speaks to their confidence in Roquan Smith to have a bounce-back season and Trenton Simpson to play a starting role, if needed, as Teddye Buchanan recovers from a torn ACL injury. Smith, 29, was PFF’s 20th highest-graded player at the linebacker position in 2025 and while earned a third consecutive Pro Bowl selection. His overall performance left some to be desired, though, for his standards. Buchanan was emerging as a steady contributor in his rookie season and, before suffering a torn ACL in December, had seized the starting role from Simpson early in the year. Simpson has been an up-and-down defender for his career so far but could have a breakout season in a new defensive scheme. He still possesses high-level athletic tools and has shown playmaking ability in a spot-starter capacity. 2. Cleveland Browns Starters: Carson Schwesinger, Winston Reid, Quincy Williams Depth: Nathaniel Watson, Justin Jefferson, Easton Mascarenas-Arnold Last year, early second-round pick Carson Schwesinger proved to be a rookie sensation. Schwesinger was a leading defensive force for the Browns and stuffed the stat sheet with 156 total tackles, two interceptions, 11 tackles for loss and 2.5 sacks in almost 1,000 snaps. His performance now has him already widely regarded as one of the league’s top off-ball linebackers. The Browns signed veteran Quincy Williams in free agency to replace Devin Bush, who started 27 games for the team over the past two years. The rest of this group is comprised of recent draft picks or incoming rookies who are not yet proven defensive contributors. The onus will be on Williams to provide a steadying force and Schwesinger to make a second-year ascension to elite status. 3. Pittsburgh Steelers Starters: Patrick Queen, Malik Harrison Depth: Cole Holcomb, Payton Wilson, Jamin Davis Patrick Queen is returning for his third season as a starter in Pittsburgh, having exceed 1,000 snaps in each of the past two years in 34 games. Queen had another productive statistical season in 2025 but analytically did not grade well once again. His PFF grade (44.0) ranked 78th among all linebackers. Alongside Queen is fellow former Raven Malik Harrison, who signed with the Steelers last year and started nine of 11 appearances. Harrison, 28, had 41 combined tackles and was PFF’s 58th highest-graded linebacker. Reserve Cole Holcomb was re-signed to a two-year deal this offseason and will enter his third season with the Steelers. Holcomb has started 11 of 22 games for Pittsburgh since 2023 but only played 645 total defensive snaps. 4. Cincinnati Bengals Starters: Barrett Carter, Demetrius Knight Jr., Oren Burks Depth: Joe Giles-Harris, Shaka Heyward, Liam Anderson The Bengals drafted a pair of linebackers in last year’s draft who immediately stepped into significant defensive roles. Demetrius Knight Jr. started 14 games and Barrett Carter started 12 games, while each playing just shy of 800 snaps and recording 106 tackles. Knight ranked No. 83 and Carter ranked No. 85 at the position in PFF grade, indicating both players have room to grow to become more efficient and consistent. Returning as well is veteran Oren Burks, who started nine of 17 games last year in his first season with the Bengals. Burks only played 340 defensive snaps compared to 385 on special teams, which with his career averages. This group’s ability to improve and play cohesively will be a determining factor in the Bengals being able to turn around their defensive woes in recent years.

Just a few weeks ago, we were talking about whether Deven Thompkins had a chance to make the Bills’ roster as a return specialist. After his release on July 14, we know that isn’t going to happen unless the Bills bring him back again later in the summer. In today’s edition of “91 players in 91 days,” we discuss the man Buffalo acquired that led to Thompkins’ release. _____________________________________________________________________________ Name: Quentin Skinner Number: Not assigned; Skinner wore 88 with the New York Jets, but that number isn’t available with Buffalo Position: WR Height/Weight: 6’5” 195 lbs. Age: 24 (25 on 12/24/2026) Experience/Draft: 1; signed with Jets following the 2025 NFL Draft College: Kansas Acquired: Claimed off waivers on 7/14/2026 Financial situation (per Spotrac): Skinner enters the second year of the rookie free agent deal he signed last spring with the Jets. If he makes Buffalo’s 53-man roster, he carries a cap hit of $885,000 for the season. Buffalo would not have any dead cap charge if they were to release Skinner. 2025 Recap: Skinner finished up his college career with the Jayhawks by doing what he did best: making explosive plays in the passing game. He averaged 19.8 yards per catch across three seasons with Kansas, totaling 80 receptions for 1,584 yards and 11 touchdowns in 38 games where he actually appeared on offense. He did not receive an invite to the 2025 NFL Scouting Combine, but he participated in Kansas’ Pro Day. He ran the forty-yard dash in 4.51 seconds, completed the three-cone drill in 6.94 seconds, ran the twenty-yard shuttle in 4.34 seconds, and leapt 33” in the vertical jump and 10’2” in the broad jump. He went undrafted in the 2025 NFL Draft, signing with the New York Jets after the selection meeting concluded. He played in all three of Gang Green’s preseaosn games, catching eight passes for 114 yards and a score on ten targets. While he played well in the exhibition season, he did not make the final roster, as the Jets released him on August 26 as part of final roster cuts. They signed him to the practice squad the following day. Skinner made his NFL debut in the regular season finale against Buffalo, and while he officially caught one pass for ten yards, he also converted a two-point try in the fourth quarter after the Jets’ lone touchdown in a 35-8 loss. Therefore, Skinner can be the answer to a trivia question, as well, as he was officially the last player to score in Buffalo’s old home. Positional outlook: Skinner is one of fourteen receivers on the current roster. Khalil Shakir, Tyrell Shavers, DJ Moore, Keon Coleman, Joshua Palmer, Skyler Bell, Ja’Mori Maclin, Mecole Hardman Jr., Trent Sherfield, Jalen Virgil, Stephen Gosnell, Max Tomczak, and Mac Dalena are the others. 2026 Offseason: The Jets waived Skinner with an injury designation on June 8 to make room for wideout Jalen Walthall. 2026 Season outlook: Skinner is the tallest receiver on the roster, and like my good friend and coaching mentor once said of our basketball players, “You can’t teach tall.” That’s certainly a solid trait and a 6’5” player who excels in explosives can help any receiver room. Does Skinner have the juice to make an NFL roster? If he couldn’t see much time with a morbund team like the Jets last season, I’m tempted to think the answer is no, but the Jets, for all their shortcomings last season, did have a fairly solid receiver group, and they had plenty of players who fit Skinner’s prototype. Could a change of scenery and scheme help? It certainly can, and while Skinner is likely to see most of his reps with the third team, the possibility of working in with the Allens—both Kyle Allen and Josh Allen—should help him, as well, given that he wasn’t dealing with a great crop of quarterbacks in New Jersey last season. At best, Skinner shows himself to be a sound deep threat who can also handle playing the gunner role on special teams, which leads the Bills to keep him as a surprise sixth wideout once the preseason concludes. At worst, he is either injured or terrible and the Bills release him. The more realistic “best-case scenario” is likely somewhere in between. If Skinner can pick up the Bills’ offense and prove that he can handle special teams duty, maybe the team cuts him and keeps him on the practice squad while he better learns the team. Buffalo may not have a top-flight receiving corps, but they aren’t so desperate where a July addition with little experience is likely to make the 53-man roster. Skinner is likely fighting for a spot on the practice squad this summer.

It’s a training camp battle that’s expected to carry loads of intrigue, where Joshua Palmer, Keon Coleman, and rookie Skyler Bell are likely to find themselves best-positioned for the opportunity. The top of Buffalo’s starting receivers chart feels well defined, with DJ Moore and Khalil Shakir in the WR1 and WR2 roles, respectively. But things are far muddier beyond them. Many will quickly point out that any conversation about WR3 also needs to carry an asterisk leading to tight end Dalton Kincaid’s involvement as a pass catcher. Kincaid’s role may supersede the production from whoever is named the Bills’ starting WR3. Even if Kincaid’s featured role wasn’t in consideration, it may be wise to temper production expectations with so much unresolved in the receivers room. More than anything else, Buffalo needs to develop consistency with their wide receivers at all levels. Have they done everything necessary to role out a more diverse group of veteran receivers? We’ll find out the answers to that only when the games count. You can be certain that plenty of hype will follow the group through training camp and preseason. It’s impossible to deny that Moore represents the clearest path at elite WR1 production since Stefon Diggs’ departure. He should draw plenty of coverage away where Shakir, Coleman, Palmer, and Bell could find room to shine. So who do Rumblers believe wins the starting WR job in 2026? It might surprise some to learn that it’s Keon Coleman, who received almost half the votes (46%). There are big expectations and a massive amount of weight on Coleman’s shoulders this season. Everyone paying attention wants to see that Coleman’s matured and proves willing to do the little things necessary to play at an elite level in the NFL. That includes all the off-field in-week prep. With a new head coach in Joe Brady as someone who said the best thing to happen to Coleman was his promotion to HC, it may be a proper reset season for the former second-round pick. In a distant second is the rookie, Skyler Bell, who earned 29% of the vote. This seems like a surprising result, simply because he’s a rookie who has plenty to work on before vaulting others in the room. It feels like Bills Mafia is high on Bell simply because he’s the new guy in the mix, and someone many hoped the team would draft. Bell will need to show out, proving to be a more reliable-hands target with a commitment to refining and deepening his route tree. In last place for these results is Joshua Palmer, who finished with 25% of the vote. This feels very low for Palmer, who brings the most experience among the trio, but who is also someone who was oft-injured in 2025. Similarly to Coleman, this should be seen as a reset season for Palmer, and you can bet he’s extra motivated to prove that he’s more than up for a featured job in the Bills’ offense. summary: The 2025 Buffalo Bills season has been written, but the book is incomplete. Before we cast our full attention toward the 2026 season, let’s take one last glance back over our shoulder for our annual look at the Plays That Defined the prior campaign. For any newcomers, first and foremost; Welcome! When it comes to […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - DECEMBER 07: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills celebrates after defeating the Cincinnati Bengals at Highmark Stadium on December 07, 2025 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Jamie Schwaberow/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2025 Buffalo Bills season has been written, but the book is incomplete. Before we cast our full attention toward the 2026 season, let’s take one last glance back over our shoulder for our annual look at the Plays That Defined the prior campaign. For any newcomers, first and foremost; Welcome! When it comes to the “rules” of this exercise, we’re not voting for our favorite highlight necessarily, but the one that best captures the essence of the game. Put differently, if you had to choose just one play to show someone to explain as much of the contest as possible, which would you choose? Week 14; Cincinnati Bengals at Buffalo Bills Buffalo had just oxidized the Steelers to move to 8 – 4. Up next were the 4 – 8 Cincinnati Bengals. While the record suggested a pushover, the struggling felines had been without quarterback Joe Burrow for most of the season. Returning to action the week prior, Cincinnati had ripped apart the Baltimore Ravens with their newly returned leader. In Buffalo, both teams repeatedly found themselves racking up points. In the end, the difference was a fourth quarter flurry by Buffalo, with points from both the offense and defense. Down 10 to start the fourth quarter, Buffalo kicked into high gear and in what seemed like moments went up by 11. The Bengals tried to fight back, but in a game where the last team with the ball seemed destined to win, the Bills made sure it was them. Bengals third-down conversion (Q1; 13:38) Plays That Defined 2025 – Week 14 – Bengals conversion pic.twitter.com/aeN9IhSACa — Kuebiko (@Kuebiko_Kami) June 24, 2026 The Buffalo Bills were VERY good in this game forcing third downs, with the Bengals facing 12 of them in total. The Bills were NOT very good once they reached this point however, allowing 10 of those third downs to be converted. This was the first of many, and it helped the Bengals establish an early lead by scoring touchdowns on their first three drives. Khalil Shakir touchdown (Q2; 7:36) Plays That Defined 2025 – Week 14 – Khalil Shakir touchdown pic.twitter.com/cLoxY4VOeK — Kuebiko (@Kuebiko_Kami) June 24, 2026 Buffalo wasn’t too shabby on third downs either for the record, converting six of 11. If you’re into math, that means Buffalo winded up facing five fourth downs. They went for it on four of those, and kicked a field goal on the fifth. Of the four attempts, they converted three of them, scoring two touchdowns. This is the more impressive, but the second half touchdown to Jackson Hawes should be mentioned as well. How Josh Allen got this to Khalil Shakir is beyond me and I watched this frame-by-frame. Josh Allen touchdown (Q4; 7:41) Plays That Defined 2025 – Week 14 – Josh Allen touchdown pic.twitter.com/fhoB66O8KD — Kuebiko (@Kuebiko_Kami) June 24, 2026 Buffalo asserted themselves in the running game, but James Cook didn’t have gaudy stats. Who did though? Josh Allen, with a lot of his day skewed by this massive run for a score. Down by ten and midway through the last quarter, the Bills needed a boost and this sure as heck did the trick. Back within three, Buffalo just needed to find an answer to the Bengals offense. Christian Benford pick six (Q4; 5:35) Plays That Defined 2025 – Week 14 – Christian Benford pick six pic.twitter.com/TeaovJXYjO — Kuebiko (@Kuebiko_Kami) June 24, 2026 At this point in the game, the Bengals had the ball six times. They scored touchdowns on four of those and punted twice. It wasn’t that the Bills hadn’t stopped them at all, but to say it was a struggle would be an understatement. Credit then to Christian Benford for reading the play perfectly and coming up with the ball for a 63-yard pick six. This put Buffalo ahead for the first time in the game. After kicking off following this score, the undaunted Bengals came right back out throwing. And immediately Joe Burrow was picked off again. The Bills capitalized on that six plays later to go up by 11. Josh Allen ices the game (Q4; 1:54) Plays That Defined 2025 – Week 14 – Icing the game pic.twitter.com/7Vn0DLJemg — Kuebiko (@Kuebiko_Kami) June 24, 2026 The Bengals were able to cut into the Bills’ lead with another touchdown. Thanks to a fumble on the two-point try, Buffalo was still up by five. With about two minutes to go, Buffalo was looking to end the game with a knee but a minimal gain by James Cook was followed by an eight-yard sack of Josh Allen. Now facing 3rd & 15, it looked like Joe Burrow would get another chance with the ball and over a minute to do it. Josh Allen put on his cape again, converted the third down, and shut the door on Cincinnati. Which play best defines the Bills’ win?

That contract is worth $1,402,500 in total. Thanks to the veteran’s salary benefit, his cap number is $1,262,500 if he makes the roster. Buffalo is on the hook for the totality of that cap number in the form of a dead cap number if Cushenberry is cut. 2025 Recap: Cushenberry began training camp with the Tennessee Titans on the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list thanks to continued rehab from an Achilles tear he suffered during the 2024 season. However, he was activated on August 11, and he managed to start 15 games for the Titans. He was called for five penalties on the year, allowing six sacks, four QB hits, and 25 total pressures. If Pro Football Focus grades are your thing, Cushenberry’s performance was not good. He ranked 36th out of 40 qualifying centers with a 55.2 overall grade, and was 39th in run-block grade (51.2). He was average in terms of pass block grade, earning a 65.5 overall grade from PFF , good for 20th out of 40 centers. Positional outlook: Cushenberry is the only player listed exclusively at center on the current roster. Alec Anderson, Connor McGovern, Sedrick Van Pran-Granger, and Austin Corbett are all listed at center/guard. 2026 Offseason: Cushenberry participated in offseason work, albeit in a red non-contact jersey as he recovered from offseason shoulder surgery. That surgery is what led the Titans to release him, as their official release was with a failed physical designation . 2026 Season outlook: On the one hand, Cushenberry was bad last year. Titans rookie quarterback Cam Ward took a league-leading 55 sacks, so that points to some ineptitude on the offensive line. On the other hand, one could also guess that Ward’s status as a rookie led him to take more sacks, whether as a result of misreading defenses or holding the football for too long as he adjusted to the pro game. This could imply that the “poor” performance of Tennessee’s offensive line wasn’t all the fault of the big fellas up front. Cushenberry hasn’t started 80 NFL games by accident, as he has shown himself to be a reliable option at the pivot. An Achilles tear limited him in 2024, and then foot, ankle, and shoulder injuries hampered him during the 2025 campaign. Cushenberry isn’t a mauler in the run game, but he has always been a good to great pass blocker when healthy. I don’t think the Bills are looking to slide Connor McGovern back to left guard, but if their starting center were to miss a game or two, the Bills could certainly do worse than Cushenberry filling in for a few games. The fact that he’s limited to center might work against him here, as the loser of the left guard battle—Alec Anderson and Austin Corbett are but two combatants—could very well end up the top reserve at center, as well. In Cushenberry, Buffalo has a great insurance policy. He could end up a top reserve, and he could also be used to obtain draft capital via trade in August if a rash of injuries impacts other teams along the offensive line. He and Corbett have essentially the same contract, and while keeping both veteran options would be nice, I don’t think it’s likely to happen. I think that Cushenberry will be the odd man out come September, but injuries and ineffectiveness from other players could necessitate a change. He’s going to be battling with three players for one spot, and ultimately, I think his lack of versatility is going to be what keeps him off the roster.

This does not correspond to jersey number, does not need to be somebody who wore a jersey, and will in no way be controversial. #55. Jeremy Chinn Panthers stats: 54 games, 50 starts, 324 tackles, 4.0 sacks, 2 interceptions Career stats: 86 games, 82 starts, 555 tackles, 7.0 sacks, 3 interceptions For many Panthers fans, Jeremy Chinn will always feel like the one that got away. Carolina selected the Southern Illinois product in the second round of the 2020 NFL Draft and from the outset it looked like they struck gold. As a rookie he started all 15 games in which he played and racked up 117 tackles. But it wasn’t just the quantity of tackles, it was the violence that accompanied them. Despite being a rookie from a small-time college program, Chinn punished opposing players who ventured into his realm. The most amazing moment from his rookie season was becoming the first player in NFL history to return two fumbles for touchdowns on back-to-back plays . As a result of his stellar play he finished No. 2 in Defensive Rookie of the Year voting behind Chase Young. It appeared back then the Panthers had found a long-term impact player. But what was also apparent was that Chinn was a “tweener” in that he wasn’t quite big enough to play linebacker full time, but he also didn’t quite have the coverage skills to play a true safety position. But the Panthers played to his strengths and he became a hard-hitting strong safety who often snuck up into the box as an excellent run stopper, but he also made Panthers fans nervous when he dropped into coverage. Chinn’s second season with the Panthers played out like his first. He had 107 tackles with a sack and five passes defended. In 2022, Chinn’s third season, he missed six games due to a hamstring injury but over 11 starts he put up 70 tackles, another sack, and seven passes defended. And it was in 2022 when the wheels started coming off for Jeremy Chinn in Carolina due to a host of absurd coaching changes and questionable defensive schemes. Matt Rhule was fired five games into the 2022 season and was replaced by interim head coach Steve Wilks. In 2023, Chinn’s fourth and final season in Carolina, the Panthers hired Frank Reich, fired him after 11 games, then appointed Chris Tabor as interim coach. In that tumultuous 2023 season, the final year of Chinn’s rookie contract, coach Reich and his staff deemed Chinn a “hybrid” player who didn’t fit their defensive scheme. He saw his playing time dramatically reduced. Chinn played over 90% of the team’s defensive snaps over his first three seasons, but in 2023 that number fell to just 39%. He also missed five games due to injury and by the end of the 2023 season, he was ready to bolt for more stability and opportunity. In 2024 Chinn was a free agent and signed with the Washington Commanders instead of re-signing with Carolina to try his luck with new head coach Dave Canales. In his one season in Washington he started all 17 games with 117 tackles, two sacks, and five passes defended. In 2025 he signed a two-year, $16.3 million deal with the Las Vegas Raiders and started off his tenure last year with 15 starts and 114 tackles. Coming out of his 2020 rookie season, Jeremy Chinn looked like a franchise cornerstone for the Panthers. As Panthers fans looked ahead back then, most of us were predicting he’d be a Pro Bowler by 2023 instead of an underutilized “tweener” mostly watching from the sidelines at the whims of a coaching staff that didn’t even last a year. As he continues to rack up 100-plus tackle seasons, many Carolina fans still wish he was doing it in a Panthers uniform.

Mandatory Credit: Erik Perel /Allsport | Getty Images Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to change that up a bit by counting down our own list of the Top 100 Panthers of all time. This does not correspond to jersey number, does not need to be somebody who wore a jersey, and will in no way be controversial. #56. Dom Capers The first ever head coach of the Carolina Panthers was obviously going to make the top 100 Panthers of all time. It was just a question of where on the list he’d end up. The answer to that question is here. It’s right here. He’s number 56. Dom Capers worked his way up from the bottom. He started his coaching career as a 22 year old graduate assistant at Kent State. He bounced around college jobs, eventually becoming a defensive backs coach, before getting his first professional football gig as defensive backs coach for the Philadelphia/Baltimore Stars. He then made the leap to the NFL as the New Orleans Saints’ defensive backs coach. He then became the Steelers’ defensive coordinator before reaching the top of the ladder. His first head coaching gig was as the first ever head coach of your Carolina Panthers. The beginning of Capers’ time in Carolina was unprecedented for an expansion franchise. He led the team to a respectable 7-9 record in their inaugural season, which is a record for most wins by an expansion franchise. He one upped that the following season by coaching the team to a 12-4 record and an NFC Championship berth. Under the leadership of their defensive minded head coach, the upstart Panthers suffocated their opponents with an elite defense and an offense that evolved into a ball control group that could complement that unit. Unfortunately, as has been the case throughout Panthers history, the success would be short lived. Cracks started showing in Capers’ third season between lagging performance and off field conflicts. Those cracks turned into a full implosion in 1998, resulting in a 4-12 season and the dismissal of Capers and his staff. Capers has gone on to serve most of the rest of his career as a defensive assistant save for one other attempt at coaching an expansion team with the Texans from 2002 to 2005. Everything came full circle in a way when he returned to Carolina in 2023 a senior defensive assistant on Frank Reich’s “all star” staff. That also didn’t end well, but coming back to Carolina always improves your standing. While Capers wasn’t able to sustain success as the team’s first ever head coach, he gets points simply for holding that title. He gets lots of bonus points for the success he brought the team in its first two seasons, even if it all crashed and burned shortly thereafter. As the first man to ever lead the Panthers to a winning record and conference championship game, Dom Capers lands at number 56 on the list of top 100 Panthers of all time.

(Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images I normally kick these Chicago Bears’ training camp positional preview articles off on offense, but the defense is where most of the questions are this year, so I wanted to begin there. The secondary and linebackers have some new faces to mix in, while the defensive line has been the chief concern from fans all offseason. So let’s start at defensive end. Roster Locks Some fans underrate Montez Sweat, but he’s an all-around good football player and also the most consistent pass rusher on the team. Austin Booker showed promise last year, and the Bears are banking on him to continue his ascent into a viable EDGE. He’s added some bulk, he’s worked on his get-off, and I feel by the end of the season he’ll have established himself as more than viable. He’ll be ready for a contract extension. Dayo Odeyingbo is ahead of schedule with his rehab from tearing his Achilles, and the Bears expect him to be the player they thought he’d be when they signed him last offseason to a 3-year contract worth $48 million, and $32 million in total guarantees. “We weren’t quite sure when we started the offseason program that we would get him for any length of time, but the fact that he’s on the field, he wants to be out there,” head coach Ben Johnson said last month via the BearsWire . “It’s just another step forward in terms of him gaining confidence again and how he’s moving. He’s done a great job of being attentive in meetings, and so I know he was really itching to get back out there with his teammates, and so it’s a step in the right direction for sure.” In eight games last year, Odeyingbo had 21 tackles, 2 tackles for loss, 1 sack, 4 QB hits, and a pass defended, which wasn’t enough. Earlier this month, Dayo attended the Sack Summit, which is a gathering of defensive linemen and pass rushers. It’s the defensive version of the OL Masterminds, where NFL players go to work on their craft. Considering he was a second-round pick a year ago, Shemar Turner isn’t going anywhere. He’s still coming back from a knee injury, and while the initial hope was he’d be back for the offseason program, now it looks like his availability for the start of camp is in question. He may need to start on the PUP list. A Good Bet To Make It Daniel Hardy provides some positional flexibility with his ability to get some emergency snaps at linebacker, but it’s his special teams skills that make him likely to stick around on the 53-man roster. Roster Bubble/Practice Squad Jonathan Garvin, Jamree Kromah, and Jeremiah Martin will again be fighting for a spot on the practice squad. All three ended last year there, and they could all make it again. Of the three, Garvin has the most experience, having appeared in 38 games from 2020 to 2022 with the Packers. The other two have yet to take a snap in the NFL. Do you see any surprise moves at defensive end for the Bears this year?

Kev’s team started strong in the early years, but has faded in recent years and is currently reworking the roster to try to get back to that early success. Let’s take a look at the roster: Let’s dive in, and let’s start with the quarterbacks. Any room that starts with Patrick Mahomes is certainly started in the right direction, and with the injury, having Justin Fields as a handcuff works well. I like the late-round pick this year of Carson Beck just to see if anything cooks there, but there’s obviously a big issue here. There’s no QB2 for the bye week. Another QB should be rostered here. Let’s be honest: the running back room is in rough shape. There’s not a lot of running backs who score many points. The young players are mostly lottery ticket prospects. There might be one or two guys you can start in an absolute pinch, but starting any of these guys for more than a week or two in a season is a massive disadvantage for Kev every week. The WR room is definitely in better shape than the running back room. Ja’Marr Chase is at the top, but I have a feeling this roster would be best served by putting Chase on the market and going to the highest bidder. Trading Godwin and Kupp would also make sense. This room needs to get younger. Carnell Tate is a good start, Golden and Worthy are there too, but it needs more. The tight end room doesn’t have much to help in the now, but AJ Barner had a nice season last year. Roush probably isn’t going to be much of a fantasy threat, especially the next couple of seasons. If Eli Stowers becomes a legit threat, him with Barner would be a nice tandem. Moving over to the defensive side of the ball, we are going to see a theme here of a lot of decent players, but not many true point scorers. The defensive line: at tackle, there are a lot of names of very good players, but they don’t necessarily score massive fantasy points. That’s tricky when finding the right tackles. 3-techs over 1-techs, always. Jonathan Allen is a penetrating DT who can score points, but how much longer can he do it? The edge room is led by Demarcus Lawrence, who still scores a solid total, but at 34, you have to wonder how much longer he can do it. Jonathan Greenard certainly can bounce back in Philadelphia; it’ll be interesting to see if he sees enough snaps to score big numbers. There’s not a lot of youth behind those two. Something this room certainly could use. The linebacker room is the best room on the defense. Bush, Franklin, and Knight are all point scorers. McDuffie is going to take a hit this year with Franklin in the mix, but Carter should still get snaps in Cincinnati. McMillan is a decent corner to have on the roster, but not a fan of the other three. In the safety room, Byard is the best point scorer here, but his advanced age is of concern. Bud Clark is the first youthful infusion here, but it needs more. Unless he knows something about Sigle that I don’t, I don’t think that’s a big prospect. The team is certainly in a rebuild. It needs a general infusion of youth across the defense, and while there are some viable WRs here, I think Kev might be in a spot where he might need to trade off his big guns for some young players or draft picks.

Doubs is only 26, and if he takes a step forward this year with more targets, he could round out a solid room. The players he has aren’t ready right now, but if they keep moving in the right direction, this room has potential for 2027 or 2028. Tight end room has Ferguson, which certainly works, but honestly, there just isn’t really anything of note behind him. This is a room that will still need some TLC. Moving over to the defensive side of the ball, I love that the tackle room has Harmon. Stewart is a startable play right now, but certainly we can question if there’s much left in the tank there. If Banks can stay healthy, he could do great in Minnesota’s defense. I like that he hasn’t overinvested in cornerbacks. Nashon Wright did score a pretty solid amount of points last year; it’ll be curious to see if he can do it again. There’s not a ton of youth in the safety room right now, but Tykee Smith is a young safety who scores, and I do like that EMW is on the practice squad. Zion Young is a young player the Edge room needs, Allen and Lane are interesting as well, and Boerkircher is also a young player for a tight end room that needs it as well. Overall, there are plenty of foundational pieces here. What this team needs is a handful of these young guys to become major point producers (Burden, Styles, etc). If that happens, Will could be a playoff team in 2027. If a couple of these young players don’t turn out as Will hopes, it certainly could delay a return to competitiveness.

He should be a good rotational and depth piece with some versatility. pic.twitter.com/Q1idIZLf4w — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) July 16, 2026 Jonathan Allen Jonathan Allen is a former first round draft selection. He has two Pro Bowls during his career, initially starting out with Washington. He spent the 2025 season with the Minnesota Vikings. Allen put up 68 tackles and 3.5 sacks last year. He has 45.5 sacks during his career. While he may not be the dominant pass rusher he once was, he still has plenty of juice to be an effective player on the defensive line. The ability to rotate with BJ Hill, while having a monster like Dexter Lawrence drawing so much attention, should allow for all of those guys to benefit from playing together. The PFF grades for Allen were poor, but the tape I watched showed a player much better against the run than those grades would indicate. He does a great job working down the line, his awareness as a run defender, and overall football IQ stand out. He is a reliable tackler, and he can still get some quick wins as a pass rusher. After playing over 800 snaps in 2025, he should be able to get that number down this season, allowing for him to remain fresh throughout the year. The Bengals also added veteran Jonathan Allen at defensive tackle. Allen recorded 68 tackles and 3.5 sacks last season for the Vikings. https://t.co/mQmOnEaOpe pic.twitter.com/ZFbrZ11hyx — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) July 15, 2026 Boye Mafe Mafe was another addition to a revamped Bengals defensive line. He was part of a deep defensive line for the Super Bowl-winning Seattle Seahawks during the 2025 season. While he recorded just 2 sacks during the 2025 season, he was still getting pressure at a high rate when on the field. You don´t have to go very far back to see more sack production throughout his career. He recorded 6 sacks in 2024, after having 9 sacks during the 2023 season. He will play a lot more snaps with the Bengals this year, and I expect a big jump back up in his sack production. The expectations should be for him to get back to being an 8-10 sack player. He isn’t a liability against the run, as some would say Trey Hendrickson was during his time with the Bengals. Mafe is a high-effort player, has great athleticism, and knows how to effectively use his hands to discard blocks. The Bengals should have a decent rotation with Shemar Stewart, Cashius Howell, and Myles Murphy at defensive end, but Mafe will be expected to lead that charge as a pass rusher in 2026. Boye Mafe is another addition to the Bengals revamped defensive line. His ability to generate quick pressures will be critical for a team replacing Trey Hendrickson. pic.twitter.com/mE5o56VWIC — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) July 15, 2026 Bryan Cook It is hard to understate just how big of an upgrade Cook should be in comparison to Geno Stone. Cook is the complete opposite when it comes to physicality and reliability as a tackler at the safety position. He is a fantastic pre-snap communicator, which has been lacking the last couple of seasons on the defensive side of the ball. The Cincinnati native should help stabilize the back end of the defense. Cook had an 83.2 coverage grade, along with an 80.1 run defense grade. He had just a 5.6% missed tackle rate last season. In comparison to Stone, who had a 50.7 coverage grade, 53.9 run defense grade, and a brutal 18.7% missed tackle rate on the season. Bryan Cook is a HUGE upgrade at safety for the Bengals defense. Physical, rangy, dependable tackler, and a great pre-snap communicator. pic.twitter.com/tbj5EyH5fF — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) July 15, 2026 Dexter Lawrence The Bengals’ biggest defensive addition, both figuratively and literally, was Dexter Lawrence. Listed at 6’4” and 342 pounds, Lawrence is a massive man on the interior defensive line. While he didn’t record any sacks in 2025, he was consistently disruptive and pushed the pocket for the Giants. Lawrence is a stout run defender who commands a lot of attention. He has a powerful bull rush, better movement skills than a guy that size should have, and had just a 5.6% missed tackle rate during the 2025 season. Dexter Lawrence commands so much attention. He takes on doubles to free up teammates, and when he is not doubled, he is getting push directly into the lap of the quarterback. Tone setter on the defensive line that will make everyone around him better. pic.twitter.com/yp0PnuN6Zz — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) July 15, 2026 With training camp just around the corner, there is reason for a lot of optimism based on the additions the Bengals have made to a defense that sorely needed reinforcements. Nothing matters until the pads come on during the regular season, but it is encouraging that the front office went out and made some moves that they normally wouldn’t.

full_text: After starring at Notre Dame, Howard Cross III now has an opportunity to prove that his size isn’t nearly as important as his relentless motor. Howard Cross III Height: 6-foot-1 Weight: 285 pounds Age: 24 College: Notre Dame Hometown: Paramus, New Jersey Experience: 1 year Cap Status Cross is signed to a 1-year, $1,005,000 contract with the Bengals, which carries a cap hit of $1,005,000 in 2026. Background Howard Cross III should have heard his name called during the 2025 NFL Draft. Instead, the former Notre Dame standout watched all seven rounds come and go before signing with Cincinnati as an undrafted free agent. Fortunately for the Bengals, draft position has never determined NFL success. Cross arrives with one advantage that few rookies possess. He spent three seasons playing under current Bengals defensive coordinator Al Golden at Notre Dame, giving him a thorough understanding of Golden’s defensive concepts. During six seasons with the Fighting Irish, Cross appeared in 65 games, recording 169 tackles, 19.5 tackles for loss, and 11 sacks. He earned Second-Team All-American honors in both 2023 and 2024 while helping lead Notre Dame to the College Football Playoff National Championship Game. His biggest obstacle has never been production. It has been perception. At 6-foot-1 and 285 pounds, many NFL teams questioned whether he had the size to consistently hold up against professional interior offensive linemen. What they couldn’t question was his effort, leverage, hand usage, and football intelligence, traits that made him one of college football’s most disruptive interior defenders. Cross spent much of his rookie season on Cincinnati’s practice squad before appearing in four games, finishing with four tackles and recovering his first NFL fumble in the season finale against Cleveland. Outlook on the 2026 Season and Beyond The Bengals have spent this past offseason rebuilding the defensive line, but there is still room for another contributor to emerge. Cross has all the tools to become that player. No one expects him to become an every-down starter overnight. But rotational defensive tackles who consistently create pressure and play with maximum effort are valuable pieces of any successful defense. If Cross can continue developing his strength while maintaining the explosiveness that made him so successful at Notre Dame, the Bengals may have found another overlooked talent who outplays his draft status.

summary: The Cincinnati Bengals went to work on fixing one of the NFL’s worst defenses from last season. They made a number of moves, but according to one analyst, it was nowhere near enough.
